Ava: Quick heads-up — weekend spike exposed our burst holdback tuning.
Miguel: saw the alert, link to grafana? :eyes: 
Ava: https://grafana.redwood/prod/d/xyz/gpu-allocs spike @ Sat 03:12 UTC, ~2.6x baseline for 8m.
Jia: I ran a short sim this morning. baseline steady_capacity=300 GPU-hours/day. With burst_max_ratio=3 we hit cold-start preemptions in eu-west-1.
Miguel: eu-west1 had limited preemptible inventory; fallback to us-central added cross-region egress and latency.
Jia: sim config:
```
steady_capacity: 300
burst_max_ratio: 2.0
holdback_window_mins: 20
spot_mix: 0.25
reserve_margin_pct: 10
```
Jia: results: 99p latency increased 18% when burst allowed >2.0x; cost delta +18% (no holdback). With holdback_window=20m and burst_max_ratio=1.6 cost +5% but tail controlled.
Ava: TL;DR we should tighten burst cap for eu-west1 and add a regional holdback to avoid cross-region fallback.
Miguel: +1. Also suggest a soft-deny signal when preemptible inventory < 12% to avoid cascading allocations.
Jia: Implemented a guard: if spot_inventory < 12% then reduce burst_max_ratio by 0.5 and route new requests to local reserved pool.
sre-bot: [alert] 1775030000 gpu-preemptible-low eu-west1 - inventory 9% -> applied soft-reduce policy
Ava: Next steps: (1) deploy Jia's policy to canary for eu-west1, (2) update autoscale runbook with holdback tuning, (3) run 7-day sim with expected Black Friday multipliers.
Miguel: I'll schedule the canary for 0300 UTC tomorrow and add cost/runbook notes. ping @oncall if anything spikes.
Ava: Thanks — keep the thread updated. :thumbsup:
